as_told.title: Lightning-scarred stone on Oshidto Ishi Hill

plain: A researcher of ancient sites named Geoffrey Drumm says that the stones on Oshidoishi Hill in Japan are struck by lightning, and that the pockmarks and melted top of one stone are scars from those strikes. He says researchers from Kumamoto University, a Japanese university, saw the stones being hit by lightning on several occasions. Drumm tells it in support of his wider idea that some ancient stones had a special link with electrical energy.
